title: Day 959: Bereaved October 7 Families Renew Independent Probe Demand — 'Refusal to Form Commission Spits on Ron's Grave'; 39 Days to Supreme Court July 1 Deadline; Election Framed as October 7 Accountability Referendum
detail: On May 23, 2026 (Day 959 / Ceasefire Day 226), bereaved October 7 families and former military figures renewed their demand for an independent state commission of inquiry into the government and intelligence failures that enabled the attack, as the Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 accountability deadline entered its final 39 days. Maayan Sherman — whose son Ron Sherman was killed in Hamas captivity in Gaza after being abducted from Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7, 2023 — publicly confronted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's continuing refusal to establish a state commission, stating: 'The refusal to form such a commission spits in my face and on Ron's grave.' Sherman's statement reflected the broader bereaved families' movement's position that tactical successes such as the elimination of Hamas commanders (including al-Haddad, May 16) cannot substitute for accountability of the Israeli government and intelligence establishment. Former IDF deputy chief Maj. Gen. (res.) Noam Tibon — a prominent figure who personally drove to the Gaza Envelope on October 7 to rescue his son's kibbutz — stated that the coming 2026 Israeli elections would be 'about the October 7 debacle, and not anything else,' framing the accountability question as the defining issue of the upcoming vote. The Knesset coalition's Kallner inquiry bill — which had passed a preliminary reading in mid-May and dropped the phrase 'full, thorough, and independent investigation' from its purpose clause — continued advancing toward a first full Knesset plenum reading expected in late May 2026. The bill, which also bars Supreme Court justices from the commission and requires an 80-MK supermajority appointment, faced opposition from Attorney General Baharav-Miara (who called it 'tailor-made for the government's personal needs'), President Herzog, bereaved family organizations, and 63% of Israelis surveyed (JPPI, May 15) who continue to support an immediate independent commission. The opposition Beyachad alliance of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid (formed May 11, 2026) maintains an independent state commission as Day 1 of any new government. With 39 days to the Supreme Court deadline, Israel's High Court of Justice had already described 30+ months without an October 7 investigation as 'unacceptable.' Any Knesset-enacted commission that does not satisfy the court's standard of independence and scope faces an immediate legal challenge.

title: Day 959: France Bans Israeli National Security Minister Ben Gvir Over 'Unspeakable' Flotilla Detainee Taunting — International Diplomatic Fallout Escalates Accountability Pressure on Israeli Government
detail: On May 23, 2026 (Day 959 / Ceasefire Day 226), French Foreign Affairs Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir was immediately banned from all French territory, citing his 'reprehensible' and 'unspeakable' actions toward French and European citizens detained aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla. Ben Gvir — who holds the portfolio responsible for Israeli police and prison services — had released a video in which he could be seen taunting flotilla activists who were kneeling on the floor with their hands bound following their detention in international waters. The 430 activists from 50 vessels had been detained by Israeli forces attempting to halt a humanitarian aid flotilla to Gaza. Released activists subsequently reported beatings, electric shocks, attack dogs, and allegations of sexual violence during Israeli detention. Poland had previously imposed a five-year entry ban on Ben Gvir. France's designation of Ben Gvir as persona non grata marked a significant escalation: France is one of Israel's most important European diplomatic partners and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly distanced himself from Ben Gvir's conduct, calling the flotilla taunting 'not in line with Israel's values' — but did not remove Ben Gvir from the cabinet. The diplomatic fallout intensifies scrutiny of Ben Gvir's conduct within the Israeli government since October 7, 2023: Ben Gvir had been consistently criticized by bereaved October 7 families and international observers for demanding military operations that would endanger hostages, for using the October 7 attack politically to argue against any ceasefire, and for screening the October 7 attack video at Israeli prisons as a punishment for Palestinian detainees. October 7 families have repeatedly called for an independent commission that would examine the conduct of all officials, including ministers, whose decisions before and after the attack contributed to Israeli failures. The France ban on Ben Gvir received widespread coverage as part of the broader pattern of Israeli government impunity that October 7 accountability advocates argue makes a credible independent investigation essential.

media.caption: France bans Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir after 'unspeakable' flotilla detainee taunts — Washington Post, May 23, 2026
